_comment: Single source of truth for the three orthogonal axes (brief §3.1), read by both the Astro site (src/taxonomy.ts) and the Python pipeline (scripts/core/taxonomy.py). Nothing in src/ or scripts/ may hard-code a section, format or topic string; it reads this file. SECTION answers 'why would someone read this?' and lives in frontmatter as `kind`. FORMAT answers 'what shape is this piece?' and lives as `format`. TOPIC answers 'what is it technically about?' and lives as `topics[]`, 1-3 per post. Decision A2 (PURE AI RESEARCH RADAR) removed the Practice section, the `fieldnote` format, and the `mobility`/`enterprise`/`selfhosted` topics from the brief's fuller draft — see the build report.

release.label: Model Updates
release.question: What is new in the model landscape?
release.blurb: A model shipped, changed or went away. What actually differs, from the vendor's own words.
release.description: New and updated AI models, drafted automatically from the vendor's own announcement. Primary sources only; press is corroboration.

research.label: Research
research.question: What have we learned?
research.blurb: Mechanism over event: how something works beats the news that it happened.
research.description: Papers, reproductions and critiques, read for the mechanism rather than the announcement. Replication failures and negative results count.

benchmark.label: Benchmarks
benchmark.question: How good is it actually?
benchmark.blurb: What the numbers say, and who measured them.
benchmark.description: A tracked set of benchmark measurements, vendor-claimed and third-party side by side, with the conditions that produced them.

security.label: Security
security.question: What can go wrong?
security.blurb: Prompt injection, agent hijacking, guardrail removal, supply chain — the failure modes of AI systems.
security.description: The security and safety of AI systems: attacks, incidents and the failure modes behind them. Reward hacking lives here, not in Research.

explainer.label: Fundamentals
explainer.question: How does this work, from first principles?
explainer.blurb: One concept, properly explained. Still useful next year.
explainer.description: One concept, properly explained, no news hook. Written to still make sense in a year.

news.label: News
news.description: A short, timely item written from the source, always linked back to it.

paper.label: Paper
paper.description: One paper, read properly, findings and caveats in plain language.

benchmark.label: Benchmark
benchmark.description: A reading of measured numbers, with the harness and conditions stated.

explainer.label: Explainer
explainer.description: One concept taken from first principles, no news hook.

deepdive.label: Deep dive
deepdive.description: One thing taken apart properly — a system, an incident, or something built and broken.

llms.label: LLMs
llms.blurb: The workhorse of the field, and the thing most coverage describes without explaining. What I care about is the mechanism underneath a behaviour, not the demo that showed it off.

reasoning.label: Reasoning
reasoning.description: Chain of thought, test-time compute, reasoning models and their limits.
reasoning.blurb: Making a model think for longer changed the shape of the field and the shape of the bill. This shelf is about what the extra compute actually buys and where it stops buying anything.

agents.label: Agents
agents.description: Tool use, agent frameworks, MCP, multi-step autonomy.
agents.blurb: Agents are where the demo and the production system are furthest apart. This shelf is about the tooling underneath — what it does when nobody is watching the demo.

interpretability.label: Interpretability
interpretability.description: Features, circuits, probing, activation steering, representation engineering.
interpretability.blurb: Opening the box rather than describing the outside of it. The closest thing this field has to a mechanism-first discipline, and the source of most of the techniques that turn out to matter later.

deep-learning.label: Deep learning
deep-learning.description: Architectures, optimisation, scaling laws, training dynamics.
deep-learning.blurb: The foundations under everything else: gradients, losses, what a network is doing when it learns. Concrete numerical examples before abstraction, wherever possible.

reinforcement-learning.label: Reinforcement learning
reinforcement-learning.description: RLHF, RLVR, reward models, policy optimisation.
reinforcement-learning.blurb: How a model gets pointed at a goal, and what happens when the goal is a proxy for the thing you actually wanted. Reward hacking itself is filed under Security, because it is a failure mode.

multimodal.label: Multimodal
multimodal.description: Vision, audio, video and cross-modal models.
multimodal.blurb: Text stopped being the whole story a while ago. What changes when a model reads a screenshot, hears a voice, or has to keep track of both at once.

training.label: Training
training.blurb: What goes in and how, which decides more about a model's behaviour than most architecture changes do. Includes the unglamorous parts: data, tokenisers, curricula.

inference.label: Inference
inference.description: Serving, quantisation, speculative decoding, caching, local and on-device.
inference.blurb: What makes a model cheap enough to actually run, including on hardware you own. Quantisation, caching, speculative decoding, and what any of it costs in quality.

evaluation.label: Evaluation
evaluation.description: Benchmark design, contamination, harnesses, construct validity.
evaluation.blurb: A score without a harness and a shot count is a number, not a finding. Methodology critique ranks well above leaderboard movement here — a contamination paper beats ten posts about who is now first.

ai-security.label: AI security
ai-security.description: Prompt injection, jailbreaks, agent hijacking, exfiltration, model supply chain.
ai-security.blurb: If you are responsible for a system, you need to know how much weight a vendor's safety claims can carry in your threat model. Attacks, incidents, and what a practitioner should actually do about them.

ai-safety.label: AI safety
ai-safety.description: Alignment, guardrails, deception, misuse, model behaviour under pressure.
ai-safety.blurb: Alignment as an operational question rather than a philosophical one: what a model does when the training signal and the intent come apart, and how anyone would notice.

generative-ai.label: Generative AI
generative-ai.description: Diffusion, image, audio and video generation, and their systems.
generative-ai.blurb: Generation outside the text stack — diffusion and its descendants. Mostly covered here when the mechanism generalises or the failure mode does.
